rule.borderline_note: Rows flagged borderline are the ones where the two readings genuinely compete. Every one carries the reasoning that decided it, so a human can flip it and rerun.
rule.not_scheme: the money runs, builds, staffs or maintains an organisation or an asset (college, hostel, hospital, corporation, board, agency, building, road), devolves general purpose funds to another tier of government, pays for the capacity of the delivery system rather than the benefit, or is an accounting or adjustment head
rule.scheme: the money buys an identifiable benefit received by a person or household: cash, a kit, food, a scholarship, a fee waiver, a pension, insurance, a subsidy, a loan, free travel, free power, a house, treatment for a named beneficiary class, or training in which the trainee is himself the beneficiary class
rule.the_line_that_did_the_work: Training is a scheme when the trainee is the beneficiary class and the training is the benefit: adult literacy under NILP and Padhna Likhna Abhiyan, skilling under DDU-GKY and RSETI. It is not a scheme when it buys the delivery system's capacity: the agricultural extension sub-mission, the livestock mission's seminars and trainings, IEC campaigns. Likewise a facility the public walks into is an institution (a one stop centre, a helpline, a home, a junior college) while an enrolled service delivered to a named beneficiary is a scheme (creche care under Palna, a mid day meal).
rule.adopted: This is the register's SINGLE definition, taken from the wording the first seven states were labelled against because it is the more carefully drawn of the two that existed. The eight states labelled later used a looser one that admitted 'a service', which pulled in the capacity of a delivery system: a helpline, a creche, an anganwadi's running costs, an agricultural extension wing. 69 published rows were re-read against this wording and 56 changed side. The register's headline number counted two different things before that and said so nowhere.

sampling: Stratified by book (SC or ST component, else Backward Classes or Minorities, else Child, else Gender) crossed with allocation band (none, and quartiles of the 515 rows that carry an allocation), 17 non-empty strata. Within a stratum rows are sorted by key and picked at even spacing, so the sample is reproducible without a random seed. Allocation is proportional to stratum size with a floor of 4, so the sample is close to self weighting; stratum_size and stratum_sampled are carried on every stratified row so a weighted estimate can be recomputed.

audit.what: Every row the classifier scores 3 or above that the stratified sample had not already covered. Together the two sets are a census of the published region, so the published list's precision is counted rather than estimated. The audit was made after the weights were fixed and was not fed back into them.

stratified.what: A probability sample of all 552 rows. This is the only set the threshold sweep uses, because precision and recall estimated on anything else would not generalise to the rows the classifier has not seen.

what: Hand labels for Andhra Pradesh's scheme-wise budget rows, a stratified probability sample plus an audit census of everything the classifier scores at or above 3. Ground truth for parse/classify_andhra.py. Audit and correct these: the classifier is only as good as they are.
